plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole streets in subtropical Brisbane turn lavender-purple as this spreading tree opens clouds of trumpet-shaped flowers. The blooms carpet pavements and lawns in violet as they fall.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late September to November, usually peaking in October
plants.funFact: Jacaranda flowers appear on bare branches before the fern-like leaves fully return. Brisbane's bloom now often arrives earlier than it did a couple of decades ago.

plants.name: Nerine bowdenii
plants.description: When most borders are fading, this bulb sends up bare, sturdy stems topped with spidery, glittering pink flowers with wavy, ribbon-like petals. The blooms shimmer in low autumn sun and last well in a vase.
plants.bloomingSeason: September to October, sometimes into November
plants.location: Gardens across the United Kingdom and similar temperate regions of northern Europe
plants.funFact: Although it is often called the Guernsey lily, this bulb is native to South Africa. It blooms with no leaves in sight, and the foliage appears later.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This glossy-leaved evergreen shrub opens the camellia year with a flush of delicate, often lightly scented single flowers. They have a ruffle of pink or white petals around a bright boss of golden stamens.
plants.bloomingSeason: October or November into December and January
plants.location: Temperate gardens in the United Kingdom, and in its native Japan
plants.funFact: Sasanqua camellias bloom earlier than the better-known Camellia japonica. Their small, tough leaves are one reason they are popular for hedges and screens.
